project.name: Reaper
project.summary: Flow-first programming language with a Python reference runtime, developing native C17 core and explicit tooling integrations in a four-project desktop federation.

capabilities.summary: Adds executable contracts for controlled runtime/target bridgeheads, stable and migratable anchors, evidence-backed baseline snapshots and metric deltas, primary/replica/fallback supporting structures, and hardware/ABI/memory-map profiles with non-overlap and permission checks; firmware staging and privileged device access remain planned or adapter-owned.

Adds executable contracts for two-dimensional coordinate grids, subsystem contour ports, deny-by-default trust perimeters, reproducible working-environment profiles and constrained workspace roots/state; OS isolation, environment mutation and filesystem workspace management remain host-owned.

Adds executable registries for normative engineering standards, policy controls and exception metadata, versioned requirement specifications with acceptance coverage, typed payload schemas with fixed-width value checks and schema compatibility, and complete row/column coverage matrices; enforcement authorities and binary schema evolution remain partial.

Adds executable contracts for reusable components, instruction blocks, typed graph nodes and topological edge order, versioned interface compatibility, and transport/protocol maturity with explicit FFI opt-in; full typed CFG/IR verification and live interface/protocol dispatch remain partial.

Adds executable contracts for an evidence-led engineering methodology, compatible approach profiles, system manifests and canonical component order, owned subsystem flows, and versioned .rpr module exports/imports/effects; compiler-enforced module ownership and effect checking remain partial.

Adds executable contracts for source/execution context and Span validation, runtime/typed value model descriptors, reusable pattern requirements, language-paradigm maturity and a cross-framework concept graph; complete source maps, typed systems syntax and compiler semantics remain partial.

Adds executable Reaper contracts for intermediate subsystem layers, ordered middleware hooks, versioned cross-project integration envelopes, bounded container profiles and embedding-host capability/lifecycle validation; live middleware dispatch, IPC, OS isolation and host syscall services remain adapter-dependent.

Adds executable Reaper contracts for target technology stacks, validated template inputs, a canonical Skeleton alias, reusable Reaper boilerplate snippets and an evidence-backed minimum language-core inventory; target builds, file generation and native typed lowering remain partial.

Adds executable contracts for the Reaper tool inventory, PATH-probe evidence, composable tool bundles, dependency-first package manifests and runtime/platform stack profiles; package lockfiles, installation and external tool execution remain planned.

Adds executable Reaper contracts for runtime lifecycle transitions, execution-context quotas and engine maturity, a capability-matched System Runtime host boundary, and versioned reusable-module dependencies; scheduler, native backend and privileged host dispatch remain partial.

Adds executable Reaper contracts for typed aggregate schemas and fixed-width scalar validation, deterministic dependency-order construction plans, the canonical four-project OCTA-8 peer inventory, capability-declared extension manifests and host-shell lifecycle/request validation; compiler-native layout, extension loading and host dispatch remain partial.

Adds executable Reaper contracts for semantic invariants, versioned compatibility descriptors, project/module roots, application composition and compiler/runtime backbone flow; complete static effect/ownership checking and native integration remain partial.

Executable Reaper module defining Scaffold, Platform, Environment, Infrastructure and Architecture contracts with validation for repository areas, profile maturity, positive resource budgets and canonical layer ordering; native target integration remains partial.
Reference lexer, parser, AST interpreter, CLI and bounded execution semantics.
Selectable Python bytecode VM over Canonical IR while tree-walk execution remains the compatibility default.
Versioned .rpr module loading, isolated scopes, cached exports, dependency graph and cycle diagnostics.
Managed resource accounting, heap and open-file quotas, deterministic cleanup and execution limits.
Consumes versioned OPlague device snapshots and exposes normalized comparison reporting.
Optional typed bridge to Pytyliki C ABI v1; native loading is explicitly gated by the caller.
Creates and inspects reference MCU projects and cross-builds with user-installed toolchains; no built-in flashing or live hardware debugging is claimed.
Reaper-written tokenizer and Pratt expression parser cover a tested subset, not a complete self-hosting compiler.
Repeatedly squares an explicit deterministic transformation pipeline by applying the same pass sequence 2^depth times.
Validates the complete four-project directed peer product, twelve status-labelled links, eight pyramid facets and four independent self-loops without a central runtime dependency.

interfaces.format: OCTA-8 octagonal-pyramid topology and peer contract

integrations.summary: Reads a caller-selected OPlague snapshot and validates its declared schema before comparison.
Uses an explicitly enabled native bridge and trusted shared-library path for metric cross-checks.
Participates in the direct OCTA-8 peer mesh; OPlague publishes device snapshots and validates Reaper comparison reports.
Participates in the OCTA-8 peer mesh through explicit synchronous Pytyliki ABI request/response.
Records membership in the shared four-project OCTA-8 topology without introducing a runtime dependency.

safety_boundaries: Execution quotas are resource guardrails, not a security sandbox for untrusted programs.
Filesystem, process, network, clock, shell and native-library effects remain explicit or opt-in rather than ambient expression behavior.
Native FFI executes in-process native code and must only load trusted ABI-compatible libraries.
The native C17 implementation and self-hosting frontend remain partial; Python is the compatibility reference.
extension_points: Canonical IR and selectable execution engines.
Versioned .rpr module interfaces and explicit import/export boundaries.
Opt-in C ABI adapters and validated versioned JSON interchange.
Native C17 frontend stages with Python reference behavior as the compatibility oracle.
Bounded vertical self-composition for deterministic compiler and data-flow transformation pipelines.
